reasons: The tests were read, not run, so passing status is not confirmed.
The fingerprint is correct only as long as the stripped keys list stays in step with the tests.

terms.meaning: a short code computed from a contract's shape, which changes when the shape changes
a machine-readable description of what a data record must look like
a test that makes a deliberate change to a copy and checks that the check notices
a field that may only take one of a fixed list of values

used_by: the pytest run for the schema tests

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Imports and purpose of the file
sections.what: The docstring explains that the version number is the one part of the contract no compiler checks. Imports bring in the fingerprint helpers and version constants.
sections.why: Forgetting to bump the version fails no other test, so this file is the check for it.

sections.name: live_schema
sections.title: Live schema export helper
sections.what: Produces the current schema of the process record model, in the form that is serialised.
sections.why: Tests use it as the starting point and then alter copies of it.
sections.watch_out: Each call builds a fresh copy, so one test's edits do not leak into another test.

sections.name: TestTheVersionMatchesTheShape (part 1)
sections.title: Version matches shape
sections.what: Checks that the declared fingerprint equals the live one, that the version is 3.0.0, that only that version is readable, and that a record on the old version 1.0.0 is refused.
sections.why: A stored record read against a contract that has moved underneath it should fail with a clear message about the version, not a confusing error about one field.
sections.watch_out: A deliberate shape change now fails until the version and the fingerprint are both updated.

sections.name: TestTheVersionMatchesTheShape (part 2)
sections.title: Old 2.0.0 confidence shape is refused
sections.what: Checks that a confidence payload in the old 2.0.0 shape cannot be read, for two separate reasons: a required field is missing, and a stored agreement value has no matching account.
sections.why: Running the old shape shows the major version bump was necessary, rather than just asserting it.
sections.watch_out: The test checks the error type for the missing field. Both reasons must remain, or the test could pass for the wrong reason.

sections.name: TestTheFingerprintMovesOnShapeAndNotOnProse (part 1)
sections.title: Fingerprint moves on shape, not wording
sections.what: Checks that adding, removing or widening a field, changing whether it is required, adding an enum value, changing a work unit value or a numeric bound all change the fingerprint. Rewording descriptions and reordering properties must not change it.
sections.why: A check that moved on every sentence would be bumped reflexively, and the docstring notes that most of the reasoning lives in those sentences.
sections.watch_out: The tests name specific fields and enum values, so renaming them will break these tests.

sections.name: TestTheFingerprintMovesOnShapeAndNotOnProse: test_a_reordered_enum_does
sections.title: Enum order matters
sections.what: Checks that reversing the order of a posture enum changes the fingerprint.
sections.why: Ordered lists are part of the contract, so sorting them before hashing would make two different contracts look the same.

sections.name: TestTheStripper
sections.title: Stripping prose from the schema
sections.what: Checks that the stripping helper removes description, title, example, schema and id keys at every depth, and leaves other keys alone. It also checks that the version embedded in the export identifier does not change the fingerprint, and that the exported schema file matches the live model.
sections.why: Prose and version labels are not shape, so they should not change the fingerprint. The exported file is what outside consumers read, so it must match the model.
sections.watch_out: If the model changes and the exported file is not regenerated, the last test fails.

summary: Tests the fingerprint, a short code computed from the shape of the process record contract, so a change to that shape without a version bump is caught.
purpose: Acts as a substitute compiler for the version number. It fails when the contract's shape changes without the version moving, and stays quiet for wording-only changes.
why: The module docstring says a forgotten version bump fails no test until a stored record is read against a changed contract, and then the error is confusing.
how: Takes the live schema of the process record, removes prose and version keys, and computes a hash. Tests compare this hash with the declared one, check the version number, confirm an old version is refused, and mutate copies of the schema to see whether the hash moves in the right cases.
inputs: The live process record model, the declared version and fingerprint constants, and the exported schema file.
outputs: Pass or fail results from pytest. No files are written.
risks: Declared fingerprints are compared exactly, so any deliberate shape change must update the version and the fingerprint together. Edits to the exported schema file must match the live model.
debug: If the declared fingerprint test fails, the message gives the live shape and the declared one. Decide what kind of change was made before updating the version. If the exported file test fails, regenerate the exported file from the live model.
